value.reason: Passwords are sent in the URL query string of a GET request and then written to a log file. The frontend (user.service.ts:54-55) builds a GET request to /rest/user/change-password with the current, new and repeat passwords added as query parameters. server.ts:636 registers that route as app.get, and routes/changePassword.ts:14-17 reads the secret values from the request, which fits reading req.query. Morgan runs in 'combined' format (server.ts:370), which logs the full request URL, query string included, to logs/access.log.%DATE% for 2 days. So plaintext passwords end up in persistent access logs, and can also leak through proxies, browser history and Referer headers. This matches the positive example (GET route, query-string password, Morgan writing to a file) and not the negative one (POST with a body). This is CWE-598, and storing plaintext credentials in logs fails the reasonable security safeguards in DPDP Rule 6(1), including the encryption and masking measures in 6(1)(a).
